title: Decision-Tree Rollout Orchestrator with Heterogeneous Metric Anchors and Gradual Fallback Latch
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a decision-tree based rollout orchestrator that selects per-cohort rollout strategies using multiple metric anchors and a hysteresis latch to avoid oscillation; instrumentation + migrations included.
description: Context and motivation: we need more flexible per-cohort rollout behavior for mixed-batch workloads across Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Current canary controller uses a single aggregated SLO that often misses localized regressions (e.g., latency spike for long-tail queries or relevance drop for rare intents). This PR introduces a decision-tree orchestrator that: (1) evaluates multiple heterogeneous metric anchors (latency P95, token-efficiency, semantic-similarity AUC, error rate), (2) selects an appropriate rollout lane (fast-canary, conservative-staged, shadow-validation, or ab-experiment) per cohort, and (3) enforces a gradual fallback latch (hysteresis) to prevent flip-flop on noisy signals. Design summary: the orchestrator encodes policy nodes as a small decision tree that maps cohort features + recent metric deltas to rollout actions. Metric anchors are configurable per-customer and composable: each anchor returns an enum (ok/warn/fail) with an associated confidence weight; the decision tree aggregates those via ordered rules rather than a single scalar. The hysteresis latch records a short-term history window and requires a sustained delta before changing the active lane; it supports manual override and emergency drain. Key changes: - control-plane: orchestrator controller + decision-tree DSL and validation schema - runtime: a lightweight policy proxy that maps incoming requests to cohort lanes and attaches lane metadata to the request context for downstream routing - telemetry: new metric anchors (anchor.*) and rollout events (orchestrator.*) + dashboards - migration: default rule set for existing customers to preserve current behavior, opt-in for advanced per-cohort behavior Checklist: - [x] policy DSL + validation schema - [x] controller + leader-election tests - [x] runtime policy proxy and context propagation - [x] unit + integration tests for hysteresis latch - [x] dashboards and alerting queries - [x] migration guide and config flag Testing and validation: local integration harness runs canary and shadow scenarios with synthetic cohorts including long-tail token sequences to validate lane selection. Load tests show no observable latency impact at 99th percentile for the proxy under normal batching (added ~0.6ms median for cohort lookup cached path). Safety behavior and rollback: the orchestrator attaches automatic rollback triggers to lanes — if a fail anchor is sustained beyond configurable thresholds across the cohort sampling window the controller will (in order) pause new traffic to the lane, divert to shadow-only, then trigger a transactional swap or full rollback depending on severity. The hysteresis latch prevents oscillation by requiring two consecutive windowed evaluations before lane transitions. Migration plan: rollout is feature-flagged per org; default policies map to existing staged-canary to preserve SLOs. Docs: migration and DSL reference added to docs/rollouts/orchestrator.md. Related work: builds on ENG-2431 (per-cohort routing) and PRs around staged rollouts; coordinates with SUP-1120 (customer incident that motivated multi-anchor detection).
